risk_reasons: The change opens the autonomy-expansion path: an Owner Operator Proposal can now widen auto-reply scope, the veto window, or the daily cap without the owner opening the auto-approval settings form.

A new transaction-aware writer, patchAutoApprovalSettingsInTransaction, exposes the auto-approval policy writer to a second caller; a lost lock, a lost exposure classification, or a lost archived-policy rule would silently weaken invariant #3.
Apply and the settings form can now race on the same account and location rows; a wrong lock order or a weak version token can commit a state the owner never saw on the card.
The Consequence line states real counts to the owner. A wrong threshold predicate or a wrong day bucket produces an honest-looking but false number that the owner uses to decide on more autonomy.
Asymmetric friction is the only barrier on an expansion card. A typed-scope check that does not compare exactly against the stored Proposal removes that barrier.
The prompt, the catalog, and the provider JSON schema all change together for the owner_operator task; a schema drift breaks live turns on staging as it did in T8.

The Consequence line depends on a new ingestion-origin marker written by the two review ingestion writers; a marker written on a losing insert, a later update, or a foreign tenant would count imported or unknown reviews as live.
goal: On the Operator screen an owner receives Proposal cards for auto-reply scope, veto window, and daily cap, each carrying a server-computed Consequence line; a card that widens autonomy applies only after the owner types the scope in words that equal the Proposal's after state, and the Receipt records the old-rule and new-rule eligible counts.
non_goals: Undo from receipts, createRestoreProposal, restoreInputFromState, the Restore button, and the rules timeline (Run E).
clear_location_override as a proposable operation (Run E).
The policy-refused card, the refusal_ref segment, refusal ledger lanes, and migration 121 (Run E).
CA1 dispatch-exhaustion coupling, CA4 lease and watchdog clocks, and the §12.1 staging items 2 and 6 (Run D).
Any database migration; the auto-approval and Operator tables are used as they exist today.
Any production feature-flag change; OWNER_OPERATOR_ENABLED stays off in production.
Changing review response generation, job enqueueing, publishing, or consent behavior; the ingestion-origin marker only annotates the existing first-insert review_ingested run step.
Backfilling, relabeling, or inferring ingestion origin for reviews inserted before the marker ships; absent or pruned markers stay unknown.
Changing the auto-approval settings form's own behavior, wording, or route contract.
Changing the publisher's live auto-approval gates; nothing posts to Google from Apply.
Changing the settings form confirmation vocabulary: its standard/all_ratings contract stays intact; Operator alone accepts the approved typed phrases.
Naming a COO-roster pilot owner or setting an observation window (human decision).
user_visible_behavior: The Operator reply can contain a Proposal card for set_auto_reply_scope, set_veto_window, or set_daily_cap.
Each of those cards shows the full effective state as before and after: star threshold, veto window, daily cap, and whether a location policy row exists.
A dial-only Proposal that would create a first location override says on the card that a new override for this location is created and names the values it inherits.
Scope, veto-window, and daily-cap cards carry one Consequence sentence computed from the account's real reviews over the last 30 days.
The scope card uses the word eligible and never the phrase would have posted.
The veto-window card adds the fixed waiting-window phrase to its eligible/held Consequence line.
The daily-cap card adds a sentence naming the busiest day's review count.
When the window holds no real reviews, the card states a zero count rather than hiding the sentence.

Consequence counts include only reviews with a confirmed live ingestion origin; the card and the Receipt state the 30-day received window and how many reviews were excluded because their origin is unknown, even when the included counts are zero.
Early after deployment more reviews may be excluded as unknown than counted; this is the owner-approved tradeoff (2026-09-13).
A card that widens autonomy shows no plain Apply button; it shows a field where the owner types the scope in words.
The server rejects a typed scope that does not equal the Proposal's after state, and the card says the typed scope does not match.
A card that narrows autonomy or changes a fact applies in one click.
Expansion cards render last in the reply and are visually separated; the screen offers no Apply-all control.
Readiness reasons appear on an expansion card and block its Apply; a contraction card applies with readiness unmet.
The Receipt states the old-rule and new-rule eligible counts and the actual number of drafts that keep their previously granted veto window.
invariants: Invariant #3: no unapproved posting. Apply changes dials only; nothing reaches Google from the Operator path, and the live auto-approval gates stay unchanged.
Invariant #9b: shouldUseMultiLocationSettings, shouldShowLocationsSettings, and canAddLocationForAccount stay three distinct checks and are never collapsed.
Invariant #11: entitlement is gated on subscriptionGrantsFullAccess, never on a raw status string.
Invariant #13: feature flags stay server-authoritative; no NEXT_PUBLIC_ companion is added.
Invariant #14: auto_approval_policies is server-owned; no client component reads or writes it.
Invariant #15: domain modules receive sql or tx as an explicit parameter; only composition roots import the singleton.
The owner_operator model schema carries no count, approval, or receipt field; the §3.4 validator keeps rejecting model-emitted counts.
Readiness never blocks a contraction.

The settings writer confirmationLevel stays standard/all_ratings; Operator accepts exactly 4 and 5 star, 5 star only, off, or all locations as applicable to stored after/scope, validates before mapping to standard.

patchAutoApprovalSettingsInTransaction keeps the same account lock, exposure classification, archived-policy rule, readiness check, confirmation check, impersonation rejection, and writeAccountAuditLog call as the current private writer.
Lock order for an auto-approval scope is lockAccount first, then the proposal row, taken before any freshness read.
The daily-cap day bucket is copied verbatim from worker/jobs/response-generation/auto-approval.ts:217; it counts grants per business per UTC day, not completed posts.
There is no committed mutation without a Receipt; a crash inside the transaction rolls back both.
A repeat Apply on an applied Proposal returns the stored Receipt and executes nothing.

Ingestion origin is a closed enum live|imported|unknown stored as ingestion_origin in the existing agent_run_steps.detail JSONB of the review_ingested step, written through the run-spine single writer in the same transaction as the actual first review insertion. No migration.
processReview with the default or LIVE_INGEST_NEW lane writes live; BACKFILL writes imported; any other explicit generation lane on a new insert writes unknown; importReview writes imported.
Only the winning insert writes a marker. A duplicate or retry that loses the insert, a content update, and on-demand generation never create, backfill, or relabel an ingestion origin.

The answered-import writer insertImportedReview pre-mints the review UUID and treats the row as newly inserted only when RETURNING id equals it; only that winner records an imported marker via startOrGetActiveRun/recordStep/completeRun in the same transaction. Its accountId is the provider account ID, never the billing tenant; the billing account is resolved through businesses.

The consequence reader counts only reviews whose review_ingested markers match the exact billing account, active business, and review on the review_handler/review subject, are nonempty, and are consistently live. Consistent imported markers are excludedImported; missing, unknown, unrecognized, or contradictory markers are excludedUnknown. Review IDs are deduplicated before simulateRule. Connection dates, later generation lanes, and missing drafts never prove live. No later response activity is used to classify ingestion.

excludedUnknown, excludedImported, and the window are server-only stored consequence fields; the owner_operator model schema gains none of them. Excluded reviews are never in total, eligible, held, or busiestDay.
edge_cases: Consequence window stays at 30 days, the spec default. If the staging account holds no real reviews in the window, the counts stay zero and the sentence stays honest rather than switching to 90 days.

A Proposal that changes one dial for a location with no policy row creates the row from the account default seed; the card explains the created override and the before state shows the inherited values.
A null star threshold means no review is eligible; simulateRule returns zero eligible and holds every review.

Imported reviews are excluded from both the eligible and the held counts, because they are never auto-eligible. Only a confirmed live ingestion-origin marker makes a review countable; imported and unknown reviews are excluded and the unknown exclusion is shown as a count.
A review inserted before the marker shipped, or whose run-spine step was pruned past the 180-day retention, has no marker and counts as excludedUnknown.
A review with multiple review_ingested step rows is counted once; conflicting live and imported markers make it excludedUnknown.
A duplicate answered import or a race between live ingest and import keeps the origin of the actual first insert.
The daily cap holds every review in a UTC day after the cap is reached, using the publisher's own day expression.
The typed scope is compared exactly against the stored Proposal's after state; a near match, a different case, or a stale phrase is rejected and nothing is written.

The form and Apply serialize on the account lock. If the form writes first, Apply becomes stale. If Apply writes first, the form may subsequently make its own valid write; the form has no version-token contract.
Two pending Proposals target the same scope: the first Apply wins, the second becomes stale on its version token.
The account default changes under a location that inherits it: the prepared Proposal becomes stale because the account default row is part of the version token.
The account default row or the location row is absent: the version token records it as absent rather than as a missing field, so an absent row and a present row never collide.
The contract_version of a stored Proposal is not current: Apply rejects with contract_changed before the transaction opens.
An expansion is proposed while readiness is unmet: the card shows the readiness reasons and Apply is blocked; the matching contraction still applies.
An impersonated actor reaches Apply: the writer rejects before any mutation, as the settings module already does.
The committed after state differs from the prepared preview: the Receipt shows the actual state and flags the difference.
Apply consumes no model call, so no new api_costs row is written for the Apply step.

verification_commands: pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build
rollback_plan: Revert through a PR and redeploy the prior build. No migration or production flag flip occurs. Previously applied settings remain ordinary audited policy rows and can be changed through the existing form. Do not claim a reverted reader understands new persisted Proposal shapes; verify this before rollback and use the flag-flip skill for an authorized staging disable if required. Production OWNER_OPERATOR_ENABLED stays off.
observability: Stored Proposals show the server-computed consequence and full effective state; Receipts record old/new counts and the actual retained-veto draft count.
Apply responses distinguish stale, contract_changed, typed-scope mismatch and readiness refusal without logging owner text.
The existing account audit writer records the policy change in the mutation transaction; Apply performs no LLM call.
Live keyed structured-task eval reports and a post-merge staging scope-card journey supply provider and application evidence.
